recipes.name: Easy Spinach Lasagna with White Sauce

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 10x15 inch lasagna pan with cooking spray.
Place the spinach in a medium bowl. Microwave, uncovered, on high for 4 minutes. Mix in ricotta. Beat the egg with a wire whisk, and add it to the spinach and ricotta. Stir well to blend.
Combine pasta sauce with milk in a medium bowl. Mix well.

Spread about 1/2 cup pasta sauce mixture evenly in the bottom of the dish. Place 3 uncooked noodles over the sauce. Spread half of the spinach mixture over the noodles. Sprinkle with half of the carrots and half of the mushrooms. Place 3 more noodles over the vegetable mixture. Pour 1 1/2 cups sauce over the noodles. Spread the remaining spinach mixture over the sauce, followed by layers of the remaining carrots and mushrooms. Place 3 more noodles over the vegetables. Pour remaining sauce evenly on top. Sprinkle with the mozzarella cheese. Spray a sheet of aluminum foil with cooking spray. Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil, spray side down.

Bake for 50 to 60 minutes. Remove from oven, uncover, and spoon some sauce over the exposed top noodles. Turn the oven off, and place the uncovered dish back into the warm oven for 15 more minutes. Serve at once, or let rest until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Spinach Lasagna with White Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Use a ready-made Alfredo sauce to layer with spinach, egg and ricotta, carrots and mushrooms, mozzarella cheese and uncooked lasagna noodles for a creamy, dreamy baked delight.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was a good base, but some variations make it excellent. First, I used mushrooms and onions and carotts. I sauteed with garlic before adding to lasagna. I also put a layer of mozzarella in the middle as well as on top. Finally, I sprinkled some garlic bread crumbs and parmesan cheese on top. This made the lasagna crispy and cheesey on top. I made this for a wedding shower and it was a big hit - even with non-vegetarians. Also, this can be made a day in advance and then baked right before serving.

This recipe was a HUGE hit with the family! I had my mother-in-law doubting it once she learned that I don't preheat the sauce or cook the noodles. But she was exclaiming how PERFECTLY everything was cooked and even went back for seconds! I varied it slightly by doubling up on the ricotta mixture using double spinach and a second egg. I sauteed the mushrooms in garlic and oil before layering them in the dish and I also threw in some mozzarella in layers that didn't call for it. Minor tweaks, added some love and it was a huge smash! Thanks for this!

I used oven lasagna noodles. Besides the spinach, carrots and mushrooms, I also added peas.
Instead of Ricotta cheese I used Cottage cheese.
Substituted the milk with evaporated milk.
I also added ground pork sausage which I seasoned with cumin, basil, oregano, parsley and added finely chopped 1/2 of a medium onion. 
I also made my own Alfredo sauce with lots of graded Parmesan cheese.
It turned out delicious and YES, I will make it again.

Made this as written and it was pretty good. Made it a 2nd time time and sauteed the mushrooms and spinach with some garlic, salt, pepper and it made such a big difference! Think it just needed that to give it a little extra "umph." Also 2nd time added veggie crumbles on top on the spinach mixture for a little extra protein and substance. Loved the ease of this recipe and thought it was a great starting point. Thanks!
The lasagna was delicious! I decided to saute the mushrooms in butter and minced garlic to add more garlic flavor, but otherwise I followed the recipe. It was so good!

The flavor was good,but I would make this more like my "regular" lasagna recipe: Instead of adding milk to the sauce, pour 1/4 cup water around the edges of the dish or use oven ready noodles. This was way too watery for me. And yes, I did squeeze the water out of the spinach. Using half broccoli and half spinach was definitely a good choice. More brown on top would have been nice as well, so removing foil at about 40 minutes would probably help. Great core recipe, just needs a bit of tweaking.

I just made this in quantity for 60 people! I multiplied the recipe times 5 and put it in two restaurant-type deep bins, maybe 12 x 20 inches and 5 inches deep, for my church group. It was a huge hit, but I did make some changes. I made the Alfredo sauce with the Quick and Easy Alfredo Sauce recipe from allrecipes, multiplying that recipe by three to get the 10-12 cups needed. Going by reviews, I doubled the eggs -- actually I used a dozen eggs instead of 10, so a bit more, to give it more cohesiveness. I doubled the mushrooms, added some chopped red pepper, added onions (used frozen chopped onions) and sauteed the veggies the night before. Note, there was quite a bit of liquid from the sauteed vegetables, and I did drain off about half of that before putting the lasagne together. That helped the lasagne hold together. I used flat sheets of no-boil lasagne, and turned out to need only about 2/3 of the weight of noodles, probably because they were flat. I used much more cheese than the recipe stated, using about 3 pounds of mozzarella inside the lasagne and 2 pounds of shaved Parmesan on top (so for the original non-multiplied recipe, this would be 1 pound of cheese instead of 1/2 cup). The shaved Parmesan on top added wonderful flavor. And when I uncovered the lasagne, I sprinkled it with Panko crumbs, per another reviewer, for a crunchy topping. What a hit! This is a great recipe!

This was a fantastic recipe. I modified it and it was wonderful. I added cubed pieces of butternut squash, yellow onion, diced broccoli, and shredded carrots, and sauteed it all together with a little fresh garlic. I then followed the recipe and added the spinach to the ricotta mixture. I used fresh spinach and just sauteed it down a little also before mixing it in. I while say the the recipe calls for you to add half a cup of milk to the alfredo sauce with ended up making it a little too liquidy and it fell apart and didn't look as pretty. I guess it depends on how thick or thin the alfredo sauce is that you are using, next time I don't think I will add milk. I also followed some suggestions of adding panko bread crumbs on top with some fresh oregano as well and it came out beautifully!

I followed this recipe as prescribed, using the Quick and Easy Alfredo Sauce recipe 
 and fresh spinach. It was good, but it lacked in flavor & seasoning. It was also undercooked as prescribed. 

I did a 2nd tray this time I sauteed the spinach, carrots, mushrooms, separately and with minced garlic, salt n pepper. Did not dilute the Alfredo by adding that much milk. Used whole grain lasagna noodles.
Kicked the oven temp up to 375
Side by side taste test,, tray 2 wins w 100 % of the vote.

This was sooooo good but I confess I made this my own recipe. I'm awful about following recipes to the letter. And I do measure some things but a lot of it I just "dump" into the recipe. What I did to this recipe, in addition to the shredded carrots, two handfuls of sliced mushrooms, and one package of (10 oz.) chopped frozen spinach, was to add in two grated zucchini, one medium size chopped yellow onion, six cloves of minced garlic, and sautéed it all in a frying pan. After removing from heat, I threw in a handful of chopped fresh parsley, added salt and pepper and some McCormick's Italian seasoning. The Italian Seasoning gave this flavor. Instead of adding spinach to the Ricotta, I layered my veggies on top of the noodles. I also added the milk, an egg and Parmesan to the Ricotta to make it easier to spread out. And I didn't add milk to the Alfredo Sauce... I used it straight out of the jar. Basically, I did some different steps that made this labor intensive instead of easy. And I added liberal shakings of Parmesan cheese when layering the Mozzarella and Ricotta Cheese to my lasagna noodles. 

I used this recipe as a refresher guideline for Vegetable Lasagna with White/Alfredo Sauce for the amounts and to make sure I didn't forget any of the ingredients. I made more of an elaborate veggie filling and my family loved it. So I can't review the recipe exactly as it was written, but as a basic recipe for a Lasagna with White Sauce and more vegetables in the filling. But it

I steam the shredded carrots for two minutes in the microwave before adding to lasagna. I just thaw the frozen spinach then make ricotta mixture. Last, I double and the Alfredo Sauce recipe on this site by Rebecca Swift and use that instead of pre-made sauce. Received raved reviews and there were no leftovers at a Thanksgiving potluck I took this too.
Left out the mushrooms. Used cottage cheese instead of ricotta cheese. Very delicious!!

I made this recipe to the ingredients listed. Don't think it is fair to change half a recipe and then give it a rating as you are not rating the "recipe". I see this so much on this site. Prep change sauteed the spinach and mushrooms instead of microwaving. Did like the results but will probably use fresh spinach the next time.
Great recipe. I made homemade alfredo sauce and par-cooked the noodles. I doubled the spinach and did not use carrots or mushrooms since my family doesnt like them.
Added some garden tomatoes and pesto! Great
Very good. But I like onion and garlic. So in they went

I changed and added ingredients from the tomato based lasagna. I added 1 tsp of salt, oregano and basil. I added 1/4 tsp pepper. I saute onions with a can of mushrooms and added with the carrots and other ingredients in the recipe. I have done it 2 times. It was delicious. This 3rd time I added parmesan after every layer of it plus the alfredo sauce.

WOW WOW WOW! This recipe was so much better than I expected! Only alterations were that I didn't combine the sauce with milk, and didn't quite use as much sauce. I might use slightly less carrots next time, but this recipe was so solid as it stands! Can't wait to make again.
Fabulous recipe that I use over and over

Was very good, with a few changes it would be 5 stars. I sautéed the mushrooms and added garlic and some italian seasoning along with salt and pepper. I also followed some other 's advice and topped with panko and some parmesan. Was delicious, brought to a pot luck and was well received.
